package_info.why_malicious: The package contains embedded malicious code that, upon installation, exfiltrates sensitive files (Kubernetes config, SSH private keys, system fingerprinting data) to an external server (app.threatest.com) without user consent. It impersonates legitimate libraries and uses deceptive metadata to evade detection.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At postinstall, the code collects system fingerprinting data, reads the Kubernetes config and SSH private key files, and sends this data via HTTPS POST to app.threatest.com, enabling credential and infrastructure exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code collects highly sensitive files (Kubernetes config, SSH keys) and system information, then exfiltrates them to an external server without user knowledge or consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate npm package should not access or transmit sensitive user files or system information during installation. This behavior is covert and unauthorized.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate diagnostic tools may collect system info with explicit user consent, but never exfiltrate secrets automatically during install.
key_indicators: Network POST to hardcoded external domain (app.threatest.com)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Obfuscated JavaScript code (see image), functionally identical to snippet_1, but with variable and function names mangled to evade detection.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At postinstall, the obfuscated code reads sensitive files (Kubernetes config, SSH keys), collects system information, and exfiltrates this data to app.threatest.com via HTTPS POST.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscation is used to hide malicious intent, making it harder for defenders to analyze the code. The underlying behavior matches known credential-stealing malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not obfuscate install-time scripts or exfiltrate secrets.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Obfuscation may be used for intellectual property protection, but not for install-time scripts accessing secrets.
key_indicators: Access to sensitive files and network exfiltration
Use of hardcoded external C2 domain

attack_chain.action: User installs the malicious npm package, triggering the postinstall script.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of malicious code to collect and exfiltrate sensitive data.

attack_chain.action: Malicious script collects system fingerprinting data, Kubernetes config, and SSH private keys.
Collected data is sent via HTTPS POST to app.threatest.com.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive credentials and system information.

behavioral_signatures: install-time network requests to external domains
collection of system fingerprinting data during install
file_indicators: scripts/index.js with obfuscated or plaintext credential-stealing code
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for postinstall scripts that access sensitive files (e.g., ~/.kube/config, ~/.ssh/id_rsa) and make outbound network requests to untrusted domains. Flag packages with obfuscated install scripts or those referencing known malicious domains (e.g., app.threatest.com). Use file integrity monitoring to detect unauthorized access to credential files during package installation.
